name: SORA-Q
maker: JAXA with Tomy, Sony and Doshisha University
def: Transformable ball shaped lunar robot the size of a baseball that photographed the tipped over SLIM lander in January 2024.
body: SORA-Q travelled to the Moon as a sphere about eight centimetres across, then split its shell into two halves that act as wheels while a tail keeps it stable. Released by the SLIM lander during its descent on 19 January 2024, it crawled on the regolith using two gaits and photographed the lander, which had come to rest nose down. Images were relayed to Earth through its companion hopper LEV-1, and the pair worked on primary battery power alone.
facts: Among the smallest and lightest rovers ever landed on the Moon
Took the image showing SLIM resting nose down
Data relayed to Earth by the companion LEV-1 hopper
specs: Two hemispherical shell wheels with a stabilising tail and two crawling gaits
Autonomous imaging sequence after release with no live control
